questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: The curve x² + xy + y² = 7 passes through the point (1, 2). For this curve, dy/dx at (1, 2) equals:
questions.explanation: Differentiate both sides with respect to x, applying the product rule to xy: 2x + y + x(dy/dx) + 2y(dy/dx) = 0, so dy/dx = −(2x + y)/(x + 2y). At (1, 2) this is −(2 + 2)/(1 + 4) = −4/5. Dropping the y that the product rule produces gives −2/5, and inverting the fraction gives −5/4.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part I, Ch 5 Continuity and Differentiability: derivative of implicit functions

questions.stem: A curve is given parametrically by x = t² and y = t³, where t is a real parameter. The second derivative d²y/dx² at t = 2 equals:
questions.explanation: Here dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt) = 3t²/2t = 3t/2. Then d²y/dx² = [d/dt(3t/2)]/(dx/dt) = (3/2)/(2t) = 3/(4t), which is 3/8 at t = 2. Stopping at d/dt(3t/2) gives 3/2, and dividing d²y/dt² by dx/dt gives 12/4 = 3.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part I, Ch 5 Continuity and Differentiability: parametric differentiation and second order derivatives

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (function)
(A) e^(3x)
(B) log_e (3x)
(C) tan⁻¹(3x)
(D) sin⁻¹ x
List-II (derivative with respect to x)
(I) 1/x
(II) 3/(1 + 9x²)
(III) 1/√(1 − x²)
(IV) 3e^(3x)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: By the chain rule, d/dx e^(3x) = 3e^(3x), d/dx log_e (3x) = 3/(3x) = 1/x and d/dx tan⁻¹(3x) = 3/(1 + 9x²), while d/dx sin⁻¹ x = 1/√(1 − x²). The factor 3 from the inner function survives in the exponential and in the tan⁻¹ result but cancels in the logarithm.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part I, Ch 5 Continuity and Differentiability: derivatives of exponential, logarithmic and inverse trigonometric functions

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: The function f(x) = x² − 2 log_e x, with domain x > 0, is strictly increasing on which of the following intervals?
questions.explanation: f′(x) = 2x − 2/x = 2(x² − 1)/x. For x > 0 the sign of f′ is the sign of x² − 1, which is positive only when x > 1, so f increases on (1, ∞). On (0, 1) the derivative is negative, so that is where f decreases; (0, ∞) wrongly treats x² as the only term.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part I, Ch 6 Application of Derivatives: increasing and decreasing functions

questions.stem: Two positive numbers x and y satisfy x + y = 12. The maximum value of x²y is:
questions.explanation: Put y = 12 − x, so f(x) = 12x² − x³. Then f′(x) = 24x − 3x² = 3x(8 − x) = 0 gives x = 8, and f″(8) = 24 − 48 < 0, so this is a maximum. With y = 4 the value is 8² × 4 = 256. Splitting the sum equally, x = y = 6, gives only 216.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Suppose f is an integrable function on [0, 4] such that ∫ from 0 to 4 of f(x) dx = 7 and ∫ from 2 to 4 of f(x) dx = 3. Then ∫ from 0 to 2 of (2f(x) + 1) dx is equal to:
questions.explanation: By additivity, ∫ from 0 to 2 of f(x) dx = 7 − 3 = 4. Then ∫ from 0 to 2 of (2f(x) + 1) dx = 2(4) + [x] from 0 to 2 = 8 + 2 = 10. Treating the integral of the constant 1 over [0, 2] as 1 instead of 2 gives 9, and adding 7 and 3 instead of subtracting gives 22.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part II, Ch 7 Integrals: properties of definite integrals (additivity and linearity)

questions.stem: The integral of x log_e x with respect to x, taken from 1 to e, equals:
questions.explanation: Integrating by parts with u = log_e x and dv = x dx gives (x²/2) log_e x − x²/4. At x = e this is e²/2 − e²/4 = e²/4, and at x = 1 it is −1/4, so the value is e²/4 + 1/4 = (e² + 1)/4. Subtracting 1/4 instead of adding it gives (e² − 1)/4.

questions.stem: Find the area lying under the curve y = x² + 2 between the vertical lines x = 1 and x = 4.
questions.explanation: Area = ∫ from 1 to 4 of (x² + 2) dx = [x³/3 + 2x] from 1 to 4 = (64/3 + 8) − (1/3 + 2) = 21 + 6 = 27. Leaving out the 2x term gives only 21, and forgetting to divide x³ by 3 gives 69.

questions.stem: The parabola y = 4x − x² cuts the x-axis at two points. The area between the parabola and the x-axis is:

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Eliminating the constant A from y = Ax² gives the differential equation x(dy/dx) = 2y.
(B) The equation dy/dx = (x² + y²)/(xy) is homogeneous.
(C) The equation dy/dx = y/x has the solution y = x + C, where C is a constant.
(D) Separating the variables in dy/dx = x/y leads to y² − x² = C.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: From y = Ax², dy/dx = 2Ax = 2y/x, so x(dy/dx) = 2y and (A) is true. Scaling x and y by the same factor leaves (x² + y²)/(xy) unchanged, so (B) is true. Separating dy/y = dx/x gives y = Cx, not y = x + C, so (C) is false. Separating y dy = x dx gives y² = x² + 2K, which is y² − x² = C, so (D) is true.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part II, Ch 9 Differential Equations: forming an equation from a family of curves, homogeneous equations and variable separable solutions

questions.stem: For the first order differential equation y dx − (x + 2y²) dy = 0, the integrating factor is:

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: The diagonals of a parallelogram are represented by the vectors i + 2j + 2k and 3i − 2j + 2k. The area of the parallelogram, in square units, is:
questions.explanation: The cross product of the diagonals is (8, 4, −8), with magnitude √(64 + 16 + 64) = 12. The parallelogram has half this area, 12/2 = 6. Using 12 forgets the half, and 3√17/2 is half the product of the diagonal lengths, valid only when the diagonals are perpendicular.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) Non-zero vectors a and b are perpendicular
(B) Non-zero vectors a and b are parallel
(C) Area of the parallelogram with adjacent sides a and b
(D) Unit vector in the direction of a
List-II
(I) |a × b|
(II) a · b = 0
(III) a/|a|
(IV) a × b = 0
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Perpendicular vectors have a zero dot product, a · b = 0, while parallel vectors have a zero cross product, a × b = 0. The magnitude |a × b| is the area of the parallelogram on a and b, and a/|a| is the unit vector along a. Swapping the dot and cross conditions is the usual mistake.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part II, Ch 10 Vector Algebra: dot product, cross product and unit vector

questions.stem: The lines (x − 1)/4 = (y + 2)/k = (z − 3)/2 and (x + 3)/3 = (y − 1)/(−2) = (z + 5)/(−1) are perpendicular to each other. The value of k is:

questions.stem: A straight line passes through the points (−2, 1, 5) and (0, 4, 9). The z-coordinate of the point on this line whose x-coordinate is 4 is:
questions.explanation: The direction ratios are (0 + 2, 4 − 1, 9 − 5) = (2, 3, 4), so a general point is (−2 + 2t, 1 + 3t, 5 + 4t). Putting x = 4 gives −2 + 2t = 4, so t = 3 and z = 5 + 12 = 17. Treating the starting x as +2 gives t = 1 and z = 9, while taking t = x/2 = 2 gives 13.

questions.stem: Taking principal values, the value of cos⁻¹(−1/2) + sin⁻¹(−√3/2) + tan⁻¹(−1) is:

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.stem: Three machines A, B and C produce 50%, 30% and 20% of the items in a factory. Of their items, 2%, 5% and 10% respectively are defective. An item chosen at random is found to be defective. The probability that machine B made it is:
questions.explanation: By total probability, P(defective) = 0.5 × 0.02 + 0.3 × 0.05 + 0.2 × 0.10 = 0.010 + 0.015 + 0.020 = 0.045. By Bayes theorem, P(B | defective) = 0.015/0.045 = 1/3. The value 3/10 is only the share of output from B, ignoring the evidence, and 4/9 is the corresponding value for C.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part II, Ch 13 Probability: total probability theorem and Bayes theorem
